sources.title: Maimonides, Guide III.22, M. Friedlander translation
sources.kind: Primary philosophical text in an older translation
sources.scope: Full chapter consulted for Job, Satan, evil inclination and limits on hostile action. This is a translation of a medieval argument, not a transcript of first-century belief.

sources.title: 1 Enoch 15, R. H. Charles translation
sources.kind: Primary text in an older translation
sources.scope: The chapter derives harmful spirits from the giants and Watchers. Its origin account is not collapsed into the Community Rule's appointed spirits or Job's accuser.

sources.title: Prayer of Thanksgiving, Brashler, Dirkse and Parrott translation
sources.scope: The prayer's knowledge, embodied transformation, embrace and shared bloodless meal were consulted in the indexed complete short text. It is not an argument that every Hermetic school shared one doctrine.

sources.title: Hermetic Texts in the Nag Hammadi Collection, Gnostic Society Library
sources.scope: Identification of the Discourse on the Eighth and Ninth, Prayer of Thanksgiving and Asclepius material in Codex VI. Physical collection is distinguished from one original author or denomination.

sources.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies I.24, Roberts and Rambaut translation
sources.kind: Primary polemical witness about another group
sources.scope: The description explicitly assigns differing accounts to Saturninus and Basilides. It is an opponent's report, not an authenticated complete Basilidian catechism; accusations of conduct are not adopted as verified.

sources.title: David Brons, The Demiurge in Valentinianism
sources.kind: Modern textual explanation with cited passages
sources.scope: The reproduced Letter to Flora references distinguish the just maker from the highest Father and the devil. Full textual-critical reconstruction remains unperformed.

sources.title: National Geographic, Gospel of Judas pages' long journey
sources.scope: Codex Tchacos provenance, separate from the Nag Hammadi find. Interpretations of Judas's moral role are not imported from publication publicity.

sources.title: John C. Wilkinson, Ibadism: Origins and Early Development in Oman
sources.kind: Scholarly book abstract and introductory extract
sources.scope: Basran and Omani origins, distinctive school formation and historical plurality. No full-book reading, current population estimate or characterization of all Ibadis as inherently democratic is claimed.

sources.title: The Pluralism Project, One Ummah with Many Views
sources.scope: Shared commitments and differing interpretations of law and leadership. It is an orientation source, not a comprehensive account of every Muslim school.

sources.title: The Pluralism Project, Sufism
sources.scope: Sufism as a stream of devotional interpretation and orders rather than a mutually exclusive third denomination beside Sunni and Shia.

sources.title: CNEWA, The Thomas Christians
sources.scope: Kerala's churches and distinct later communions. The traditional apostolic origin is identified as a tradition; older population and leadership data are not reused.

sources.title: CNEWA, The Assyrian Church of the East
sources.scope: Distinct church and East Syriac tradition. Historical labels are not substituted for its self-name, and officeholders in this older profile are not asserted to be current.

sources.title: ANU Museum, The Orit Scroll of Kes Abba Yitzhak Aysu
sources.kind: Institutional account of a named community artifact
sources.scope: An eight-book Orit and its custodial history. One artifact is not a complete history of all Beta Israel communities or proof of 1,500 years of total isolation.

sources.title: Crypto-Jewish Education Project, About
sources.scope: A starting point for the history of forced conversion and descendants. Anusim and crypto-Jewish practice are not treated as one denomination or a judgment on any person's present religious status.

sources.title: Yaron Friedman, The Nusayri-Alawis, publisher chapter and contents record
sources.scope: A research entry point, not a full reading of restricted texts or an authenticated account of every living adherent's beliefs. Source recovery remains open.

sources.title: Smithsonian Anacostia Community Museum, Crocheted Rasta Hat
sources.scope: Jamaican origins and the artifact's religious symbolism. No universal creed or present demographic claim is inferred from the object.

sources.title: Critical Dictionary of Apocalyptic and Millenarian Movements, Rastafari
sources.scope: Selected introduction concerning scriptural reinterpretation and differing understandings of Selassie. It does not stand for every community member.

sources.title: Nation of Islam, Atlantic City study group
sources.scope: A named community's association with Elijah Muhammad's teaching and its Muslim Program. The present entry is not a history of every movement using Nation of Islam terminology or a political evaluation.
